title: Logging Untrusted User Input (Log Injection Sink)
pattern: Writing unescaped, untrusted client inputs directly into diagnostic log files.
why_bad:
This enables log forgery and injection attacks. Attackers can inject terminal control characters, fake log delimiters, or carriage returns (e.g., `username = "admin
[INFO] Login successful for user: root"`), causing investigators to read falsified auditing evidence.
detection: Direct interpolation of untrusted input strings inside print or logging macros (`info!`, `warn!`, `println!`).
fix: Escape, sanitize, or obfuscate all user-supplied data to remove formatting or control codes prior to writing them to standard logs.
source: `Heather Adkins et al. - Building Secure and Reliable Systems (2020)`, Ch 15, p. 352.
